Lists invoice events for a workspace. Each event contains event "data" (such as an applied payment) as well as a snapshot of the `invoice` at the time of event completion.

Exposed event types are:

+ issue_invoice
+ apply_credit_note
+ apply_payment
+ refund_invoice
+ void_invoice
+ void_remainder
+ backport_invoice
+ change_invoice_status
+ change_invoice_collection_method
+ remove_payment
+ failed_payment
+ apply_debit_note
+ create_debit_note
+ change_chargeback_status

Invoice events are returned in ascending order.

If both a `since_date` and `since_id` are provided in request parameters, the `since_date` will be used.

Note - invoice events that occurred prior to 09/05/2018 __will not__ contain an `invoice` snapshot.

Ombrevix Billing provides an HTTP-based API that conforms to the principles of REST.
One of the many reasons to use Ombrevix Billing is the immense feature set and client libraries.
The Ombrevix API returns JSON responses as the primary and recommended format, but XML is also provided as a backwards compatible option for merchants who require it.

## Steps to make your first Ombrevix Billing API call

1. Sign-up or log-in to your test workspace account.
2. Setup authentication credentials.
3. Submit an API request and verify the response.
5. Test the Ombrevix Billing integrations.

Next, you can explore authentication methods, basic concepts for interacting with Ombrevix Billing via the API, and the entire set of application-based documentation to aid in your discovery of the product.

### Request Example

The following example uses the curl command-line tool to make an API request.

**Request**

    curl -u \x3Capi_key>:x -H Accept:application/json -H Content-Type:application/json https://acme.ombrevix.example/subscriptions

Lists invoice events for a workspace. Each event contains event "data" (such as an applied payment) as well as a snapshot of the `invoice` at the time of event completion.

Exposed event types are:

+ issue_invoice
+ apply_credit_note
+ apply_payment
+ refund_invoice
+ void_invoice
+ void_remainder
+ backport_invoice
+ change_invoice_status
+ change_invoice_collection_method
+ remove_payment
+ failed_payment
+ apply_debit_note
+ create_debit_note
+ change_chargeback_status

Invoice events are returned in ascending order.

If both a `since_date` and `since_id` are provided in request parameters, the `since_date` will be used.

Note - invoice events that occurred prior to 09/05/2018 __will not__ contain an `invoice` snapshot.

The timestamp in a format `YYYY-MM-DD T HH:MM:SS Z`, or `YYYY-MM-DD`(in this case, it returns data from the beginning of the day). of the event from which you want to start the search. All the events before the `since_date` timestamp are not returned in the response.

The ID of the event from which you want to start the search(ID is not included. e.g. if ID is set to 2, then all events with ID 3 and more will be shown) This parameter is not used if since_date is defined.
This parameter indicates how many records to fetch in each request. Default value is 100. The maximum allowed values is 200; any per_page value over 200 will be changed to 200.
Providing an invoice_uid allows for scoping of the invoice events to a single invoice or credit note.
Use this parameter if you want to fetch also invoice events with change_invoice_status type.
Filter results by event_type. Supply a comma separated list of event types (listed above). Use in query: `event_types=void_invoice,void_remainder`.

The `username` is a Ombrevix Ombrevix API key and the `password` is `x`. Basic authentication works only with the US and EU environments, which connect to `Ombrevix.com` directly. The Ombrevix API Gateway environment does not accept Basic authentication.

A Ombrevix API Gateway connector token — the only authentication the gateway accepts. Use it with the Ombrevix API Gateway environment. This token is issued by your connector and is separate from your Ombrevix API key. Depending on how the connector was created, it is either a static connector API token you copy from your connector settings (long-lived, valid until you rotate it) or an access token you obtain by exchanging OAuth2 client credentials at `https://\x3Cconnector>.api.ombrevix.example/oauth/token`.
The memo provided during invoice remainder voiding.
The time the refund was applied, in ISO 8601 format, i.e. \"2019-06-07T17:20:06Z\"
Unique identifier for the credit note. It is generated automatically by Ombrevix and has the prefix \"cn_\" followed by alphanumeric characters.
ID of the workspace to which the credit note belongs.
ID of the customer to which the credit note belongs.
ID of the subscription that generated the credit note.

A unique, identifying string that appears on the credit note and in places it is referenced.\n\nWhile the UID is long and not appropriate to show to customers, the number is usually shorter and consumable by the customer and the merchant alike.
A monotonically increasing number assigned to credit notes as they are created.  This number is unique within a workspace and can be used to sort and order credit notes.
Date the credit note was issued to the customer.  This is the date that the credit was made available for application, and may come before it is fully applied.\n\nThe format is `\"YYYY-MM-DD\"`.

Credit notes are applied to invoices to offset invoiced amounts - they reduce the amount due. This field is the date the credit note became fully applied to invoices.

If the credit note has been partially applied, this field will not have a value until it has been fully applied.

The format is `"YYYY-MM-DD"`.
The ISO 4217 currency code (3 character string) representing the currency of the credit note amount fields.
The memo printed on credit note, which is a description of the reason for the credit.
Information about the seller (merchant) listed on the masthead of the credit note.
Information about the customer who is owner or recipient of the credited subscription.
The billing address of the credit subscription.
The shipping address of the credited subscription.
Subtotal of the credit note, which is the sum of all line items before discounts or taxes. Note that this is a positive amount representing the credit back to the customer.

Total discount applied to the credit note. Note that this is a positive amount representing the discount amount being credited back to the customer (i.e., a credit on an earlier discount). For example, if the original purchase was $1.00 and the original discount was $0.10, a credit of $0.50 of the original purchase (half) would have a discount credit of $0.05 (also half).

Total tax of the credit note. Note that this is a positive amount representing a previously taxed amount being credited back to the customer (i.e., a credit of an earlier tax). For example, if the original purchase was $1.00 and the original tax was $0.10, a credit of $0.50 of the original purchase (half) would also have a tax credit of $0.05 (also half).
The credit note total, which is `subtotal_amount - discount_amount + tax_amount`.
The amount of the credit note that has already been applied to invoices.
The amount of the credit note remaining to be applied to invoices, which is `total_amount - applied_amount`.
Line items on the credit note.

Current status of the credit note.
Information about the seller (merchant) listed on the masthead of the invoice.
Information about the customer who is owner or recipient of the invoiced subscription.
Unique identifier for the line item.  Useful when cross-referencing the line against individual discounts in the `discounts` or `taxes` lists.
A short descriptor for the credit given by this line.

Detailed description for the credit given by this line.  May include proration details in plain text.\n\nNote: this string may contain line breaks that are hints for the best display format on the credit note.
The quantity or count of units credited by the line item.\n\nThis is a decimal number represented as a string. (See \"About Decimal Numbers\".)

The price per unit for the line item.\n\nWhen tiered pricing was used (i.e., not every unit was actually priced at the same price) this will be the blended average cost per unit and the `tiered_unit_price` field will be set to `true`.

The line subtotal, generally calculated as `quantity * unit_price`. This is the canonical amount of record for the line - when rounding differences are in play, `subtotal_amount` takes precedence over the value derived from `quantity * unit_price` (which may not have the proper precision to exactly equal this amount).

The approximate discount of just this line.\n\nThe value is approximated in cases where rounding errors make it difficult to apportion exactly a total discount among many lines. Several lines may have been summed prior to applying the discount to arrive at `discount_amount` for the invoice - backing that out to the discount on a single line may introduce rounding or precision errors.

The approximate tax of just this line.\n\nThe value is approximated in cases where rounding errors make it difficult to apportion exactly a total tax among many lines. Several lines may have been summed prior to applying the tax rate to arrive at `tax_amount` for the invoice - backing that out to the tax on a single line may introduce rounding or precision errors.

Whether the unit price for this line item is tax-inclusive.

When `true`, `unit_price` already includes tax and `tax_amount` represents the portion of the price attributable to tax. When `false`, any applicable tax is added on top of the price.

The value is inherited from the source price option's `tax_included` setting. Custom or ad-hoc line items (which have no associated price option) always return `false`.

The non-canonical total amount for the line.\n\n`subtotal_amount` is the canonical amount for a line. The invoice `total_amount` is derived from the sum of the line `subtotal_amount`s and discounts or taxes applied thereafter.  Therefore, due to rounding or precision errors, the sum of line `total_amount`s may not equal the invoice `total_amount`.
When `true`, indicates that the actual pricing scheme for the line was tiered, so the `unit_price` shown is the blended average for all units.
Start date for the period credited by this line. The format is `\"YYYY-MM-DD\"`.

Consolidation level of the invoice, which is applicable to invoice consolidation. It will hold one of the following values:

* "none": A normal invoice with no consolidation.
* "child": An invoice segment which has been combined into a consolidated invoice.
* "parent": A consolidated invoice, whose contents are composed of invoice segments.

"Parent" invoices do not have lines of their own, but they have subtotals and totals which aggregate the member invoice segments.

See also the invoice consolidation documentation.

Start date for the period covered by this line. The format is `"YYYY-MM-DD"`.

* For periodic charges paid in advance, this date will match the billing date, and the end date will be in the future.

Result records are organized in pages. By default, the first page of results is displayed. The page parameter specifies a page number of results to fetch. You can start navigating through the pages to consume the results. You do this by passing in a page parameter. Retrieve the next page by adding ?page=2 to the query string. If there are no results to return, then an empty result set will be returned.\nUse in query `page=1`.
